events.text: One more angle before the access-rules guide reports back. What the terminal offers can also hinge on session state on this box — a stale recorded session, or a session-lifecycle hook, can keep the CLI from refreshing the model list it shows. Let me map how sessions are recorded here: where they're stored, where your shell history lands, and whether anything fires on session start or stop.

events.command:
echo "-- host owning these session records --"; hostname
echo ""; echo "-- ~/.claude/projects (recorded sessions) --"; ls -la ~/.claude/projects 2>/dev/null | head -20
echo ""; echo "-- shell history location --"; echo "HISTFILE=${HISTFILE:-<unset>}"; echo "SHELL=$SHELL"
echo ""; echo "-- session-lifecycle hooks --"; grep -i hook ~/.claude/settings.json 2>/dev/null || echo "(no hooks configured)"
